answer.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ, signaling that the core funnel has degraded. Memory_86 and memory_31 show that simplification directly lifts both completion rates and first-week activation. Verifying memory_86 (shortening onboarding) and memory_73 (discount trap risk) is prudent: the first confirms the mechanism we want to replicate; the second reminds us why discount-chasing would be strategically wrong despite competitive pressure. Simplifying onboarding is durable, attacks the immediate metric decline, and aligns with our primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. It avoids the retention risk flagged in memory_73 and builds on proven playbooks (memory_31, memory_91). Referral incentives (memory_57) could add revenue but require established customer base and don't fix the activation gap. Promotional pricing risks margin and retention. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is sound but doesn't address SMB activation loss. A standard experiment on onboarding simplification is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk choice given current constraints and the archive record.
